instructions: Scrub the 2 potatoes and wrap each one in a damp paper towel. Microwave them on high for 8 to 10 minutes, turning them over halfway, until a fork slides easily into the thickest part.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, stir the 3 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp sugar and 3 tbsp mirin until the sugar dissolves.
Cut the nori sheet into 8 strips.
When the potatoes are cool enough to hold, peel off the skins and mash the flesh in a bowl until there are no lumps.

Add the 4 tbsp potato starch and 2 tbsp of the milk and mix until it comes together into a soft dough. If it's crumbly, mix in the last 2 tbsp milk a little at a time. It's ready when it holds its shape without sticking to your hands.
Divide the dough into 8 even pieces, roll each into a ball and press it into a patty about 1/2 inch thick.
Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 4 patties and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is golden brown.
Flip them and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden. Transfer them to a plate. Melt the last 1 tbsp butter and cook the other 4 patties the same way.
Return all the patties to the pan and turn off the heat. Pour in the sauce, then put the pan back on medium heat.
Let it bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, turning the patties, until the sauce thickens into a shiny glaze that coats them.
Wrap a nori strip around each one and serve warm.
method_notes: All three versions mash cooked starchy potato with potato starch, shape it into patties, pan fry them golden and coat them in soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Okonomi Kitchen (the lead) microwaves the potatoes, loosens the dough with a little milk, fries in butter and glazes the patties in the pan, then wraps them in nori; Two Plaid Aprons does much the same, and Chef JA Cooks steams the potatoes and thickens a separate sauce with starch. The lead uses vegan butter, non-dairy milk and a splash of sake; this uses dairy butter and milk and swaps the sake for more mirin, which the lead allows. Optional cheese fillings are left out.
